reasoning: Both sets cover all three stages with a shared core, beats-baseline verdicts built with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, replays and lab notes. Set B is the stronger plan for learning RL. Its ladders add one idea per rung: a lookup table on the compact view, then on a 6x6 raw grid, then a network; REINFORCE before PPO; P1 to P5 with an opponent pool and cross-play forgetting counts. It cuts milestones along real dependency lines (the tank depends on M1, not M2) and freezes every M1 boundary in a single interface task. Its golden cases are very precise and check out arithmetically. Set B pays for this in bulk: a 47KB spec, packets of about 50KB that carry the whole tests.md, replan history, and a few stale or inconsistent lines (out-of-scope still says 'only what Snake and the tank need', rebuild returns bool in the contract but Replay in the pipeline, AD-13 says both 6 and five pipelines). Set A is leaner and better packaged: four layered packages, small per-package pipelines and short packets. But its milestones are less clean. M2 bundles the DQN, the lab note and the library comparison, M3 carries the replay upgrades, and M3 depends on M2's comparison. Its M1 also has build-breaking gaps: RunWriter has no snapshot method although M1-T10 must save snapshots through it, M1-T17 needs the chain2 test world that only M1-T21 writes, and the packets leave out the Learner/Transition protocol and the full-view encoding. On balance B's content is stronger, and its structure is only slightly weaker.
